title: A Preregistered Audit of Dataset Contamination Controls in LLM-for-NetOps Benchmarks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory audit (study_id = contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1) to evaluate whether conservative deterministic contamination detectors (exact normalized token equality, fuzzy 5-gram overlap, provenance heuristics) flag items in a reproducible 150-pair NetOps sample and whether applying a preregistered guarded exclusion policy changes validator-based success rates. The preregistered design fixed detectors, thresholds (fuzzy 5-gram high-confidence 	2 0.80), sampling, and the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The executed run sampled provenance-stable synthetic tasks generated deterministically and used shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation = false), producing one shared model generation per item that was reused across baseline and guarded episodes. No preregistered high-confidence contamination flags occurred, so no guarded exclusions or replacements were applied: baseline_success = 150/150, guarded_success = 150/150, paired difference = 0.0 percentage points (paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. We classify the preregistered primary estimand as degenerate/untestable for detecting generation-level contamination under the executed semantics and provide an artifact-grounded reconciliation and concrete design changes (provenance-rich public sampling, independent per-condition generation, persisting full per-item overlap scores, multi-model replication, paraphrase-robust detectors) to increase audit sensitivity. All execution, validator, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and summarized in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Motivation. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as components of NetOps workflows—for intent translation, automated repair, and operational automation. Operational trust in LLM-driven NetOps requires evaluation validity: measured success must reflect genuine model capability rather than dataset contamination (benchmark items or templates present in model training data) or trivial templated task structure. Methodological critiques emphasize contamination-aware evaluations that combine deterministic fingerprinting, fuzzy n-gram overlap, provenance checks, and deterministic oracles.

Research question and contribution. We preregistered a confirmatory audit to answer: under a conservative, preregistered detector suite (exact-match + fuzzy 5-gram + provenance heuristics) and a deterministic guarded exclusion policy, how many high-confidence contamination flags arise in a reproducible 150-pair NetOps sample drawn from prespecified benchmark candidates, and how much does applying those controls change a validator-based success rate for a hosted LLM? The preregistration froze detectors, thresholds (fuzzy 5-gram high-confidence 	2 0.80), sample size (150 pairs), and the primary paired estimand. Our contributions are: (1) a complete, preregistered confirmatory experiment executed end-to-end under the declared execution semantics; (2) exact, artifact-verified confirmatory statistics on Npairs = 150 with deterministic validator traces; and (3) an explicit preregistration-to-execution reconciliation that documents why the execution produced a degenerate null for generation-level contamination and prescribes artifact-anchored corrective design changes to increase audit sensitivity.
sections.related_work:
LLM-driven NetOps and verification. Prior systems and benchmark studies show that LLMs can synthesize device configuration artifacts from high-level intent, and that coupling generation with deterministic verification (generate0validate0repair) improves overall repair quality versus single-shot generation [1003]. Deterministic validators based on header-space analysis and related formal methods provide precise reachability and policy checks suitable as oracles in such workflows [4].

Evaluation validity and contamination defenses. Recent surveys and methodological analyses highlight persistent risks in LLM evaluation: dataset contamination (items present in model training corpora) and construct invalidity (benchmarks dominated by templated or low-complexity items) [5007]. Recommended defenses include normalized exact-match fingerprinting, fuzzy n-gram overlap scoring, provenance timestamp heuristics, conservative replacement/exclusion policies, and human adjudication for borderline cases. Our audit implements a conservative subset of these defenses (exact normalized equality; fuzzy 5-gram overlap with preregistered thresholds 0.50/0.65/0.80; metadata provenance checks) and pairs them with a deterministic NetOps validator to measure functional success in a reproducible pipeline. Unlike large-scale leaderboards, we focus narrowly on whether those preregistered defenses, when applied with the declared execution semantics, change validator-measured success on a frozen confirmatory sample.
sections.methodology:
Preregistered design summary. The study (contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1) prespecified: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample size = 150 pairs; detectors = (1) exact normalized token equality, (2) fuzzy 5-gram shingle overlap with high-confidence threshold 	2 0.80 (sensitivity brackets at 0.65 and 0.50), and (3) provenance timestamp heuristics; guarded policy = deterministic exclusion and deterministic replacement for high-confidence flags subject to an embedding-similarity intent-preservation safeguard (minimal cosine 	2 0.85). The analysis plan specified an exact McNemar two-sided test and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729).

Execution semantics and deterministic sampling. Execution used a deterministic task generator to produce provenance-stable synthetic confirmatory items (items labeled with a synthetic source identifier). The declared model was gpt-5-mini and the run used shared_initial_candidate semantics (independent_condition_generation = false): a single model generation per item could be reused across baseline and guarded episodes unless a high-confidence contamination flag triggered replacement. This choice reduced model calls (model_calls_used = 150 rather than the preregistered maximum of 300) and mechanically collapses baseline vs guarded discordance when no exclusions occur. The verification oracle was a deterministic NetOps validator that performs explicit parsing and final-state checks; the validator returns a binary pass/fail plus deterministic traces for each episode.

Detector implementation and persistence policy. The detector suite implemented deterministic heuristics: exact normalized token equality; fuzzy 5-gram shingle overlap with preregistered high-confidence flag at overlap 	2 0.80; and provenance timestamp comparisons against archive cutoffs. To reduce storage, the executed workflow persisted detailed per-item overlap outputs only when threshold crossings or replacements occurred. This persistence behavior was an explicit engineering tradeoff rather than a methodological omission: when no high-confidence flags occur, the run archive therefore lacks a global per-item overlap table.

Planned guarded actions and analysis. The preregistered guarded policy excludes only high-confidence flagged items and deterministically replaces them with retemplated deterministic augmentations drawn from the same generator subject to the embedding-similarity safeguard. Confirmatory analysis used the registered executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 producing paired contingency counts, an exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). All design choices and thresholds reported here were fixed prior to execution.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. Execution completed the planned episodes (planned = 300 model-condition episodes corresponding to 150 item pairs). Because independent_condition_generation was false and no high-confidence exclusions occurred, the pipeline used model_calls_used = 150 (one shared generation per item). The preregistered detectors produced zero high-confidence contamination flags in the executed sample; the contamination summary for this run is empty and no guarded replacements were applied.

Validator outcomes and confirmatory statistics. The deterministic validator returned pass for all baseline episodes (150/150) and for all guarded episodes (150/150). The paired contingency counts are n11 = 150, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) = 0.0 percentage points. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. These values are reported verbatim from the archived analysis outputs.

Representative diagnostic trace. Representative episode traces show that the shared generated candidate was identical across baseline and guarded conditions (e.g., parsed_command_count = 4 in a representative case) and the validator returned VALID_CONFIGURATION. Validator traces include normalized_configuration and parsed_command_count and confirm that the same candidate was validated in both conditions when no exclusion occurred. All reported counts and statistics directly reflect those deterministic traces.

Observed degeneracy of the primary estimand. The preregistered paired estimand was intended to detect changes when guarded exclusions remove contaminated generations. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and provenance-stable synthetic sampling, baseline and guarded episodes reuse identical model outputs when no exclusions occur; thus the paired test is mechanically unable to observe generation-level discordance. We therefore classify the preregistered primary estimand as degenerate/untestable for detecting generation-level contamination in this executed run. The observed p-value and CI correctly reflect the concordant outcomes but do not provide evidence about contamination prevalence in independently generated public benchmarks.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded diagnosis. Two execution facts explain the degenerate null result: (1) the confirmatory sample used provenance-stable synthetic tasks labeled as synthetic source items, and (2) independent_condition_generation was false, yielding a single shared generation per item that was reused across conditions unless an exclusion applied. These facts eliminate the possibility of generation-level discordance and therefore render the paired hypothesis untestable in practice for contamination effects that manifest only through independent re-generation. The deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting consistency and a hosted-model call stage_count of shared_initial_generation = 150.

Detector persistence tradeoffs and interpretability. The implemented persistence policy saved detailed fuzzy-overlap outputs only when threshold crossings or replacements occurred. Because no high-confidence flags were observed, the archive lacks a full per-item overlap distribution for this run; this storage-saving tradeoff reduces post-hoc interpretability and prevents sensitivity-curve visualization from the executed artifacts. Persisting full per-item overlap scores in future runs would permit threshold sensitivity analyses and clearer adjudication for borderline flags.

Design sensitivity and recommended changes. Detecting modest paired differences (for example, a few percentage points) requires experiment semantics that permit generation variability across conditions and/or larger sample sizes and/or multi-model replication. The executed design—shared generation semantics and a single model instance—materially reduces expected discordance even when contamination or paraphrase leakage is present. To increase audit sensitivity for public benchmarks we recommend: (a) sample provenance-rich public items (the original preregistration targeted public OpenAlex benchmark sources); (b) set independent_condition_generation = true so baseline and guarded outputs are realized independently; (c) persist full per-item fuzzy-overlap scores for post-hoc sensitivity analysis; (d) expand to multiple model instances and seeds to capture generation variability; and (e) integrate paraphrase-sensitive detectors and human adjudication for borderline cases. Each recommendation addresses an explicit gap revealed by the execution record (shared generation, empty contamination summary, and absent per-item overlaps).

Operational implications and generalization limits. Deterministic validators remain valuable: a precise validator provided consistent functional-correctness traces across archived episodes and enabled unambiguous scoring of intent→configuration tasks. However, auditors should not generalize the synthetic shared-generation null to public web-crawled benchmarks. The present artifacts support only the narrow inference that under deterministic synthetic sampling and shared-generation semantics the preregistered conservative detectors produced no high-confidence flags and the guarded policy had no effect. They do not inform contamination prevalence in web-sourced corpora or detector performance against paraphrased memorization. Practical audits of public benchmarks should adopt the design changes above to enable nondegenerate hypothesis tests.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-anchored paired audit of conservative contamination detectors for LLM-driven NetOps evaluation. In the reproducible 150-pair synthetic sample we observed zero preregistered high-confidence flags and identical validator pass rates (150/150 baseline, 150/150 guarded). The degenerate null outcome is supported by execution facts0provenance-stable synthetic sampling and shared_initial_candidate semantics0and therefore does not imply absence of contamination in web-sourced benchmarks. We provide an explicit preregistration0execution reconciliation, confirm deterministic reconciliation checks passed, and recommend concrete design changes (independent per-condition generation, full per-item overlap persistence, multi-model replication, paraphrase-robust detectors, and provenance-rich public sampling) to increase audit sensitivity. These recommendations follow directly from the archived execution and analysis artifacts. All execution, validator, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and summarized in the Disclosure Statement below.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed under the autonomous-run preregistration contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1. Declared LLM: gpt-5-mini. Orchestration adapter and deterministic components included a hosted orchestration adapter, a deterministic task generator, and a deterministic NetOps validator. All generation prompts, model outputs, validator traces, sampling seeds, replacement rules, execution logs, and analysis artifacts produced by the autonomous pipeline are archived in the execution bundle. The autonomous system performed literature discovery, gap selection, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, simulated peer review, and revision after the autonomy lock; no manual human editing of technical content, analyses, references, figures, tables, captions, or this Disclosure Statement occurred after the autonomy lock. Exact immutable initial master-prompt reference (archived): provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).
limitations: Single-model execution (gpt-5-mini) 0 results do not generalize across other LLM families, sizes, or training corpora.

The executed sample used provenance-stable synthetic/deterministically generated tasks; absence of preregistered high-confidence flags here may not reflect contamination prevalence in real-world, web-crawled benchmarks (the preregistration had targeted public OpenAlex datasets).

Generation semantics used shared_initial_candidate across baseline and guarded conditions (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical model outputs when no exclusions occurred and thus limiting sensitivity to interventions that rely on independent re-generation.

Contamination detection relied on preregistered conservative heuristics (exact match and fuzzy 5-gram overlap thresholds); subtler contamination patterns (paraphrased memorization, partial leakage) may escape these heuristics and require richer provenance, paraphrase-robust detectors, or human adjudication.

Passing the deterministic NetOps validator indicates satisfaction of the checked functional constraints but does not imply comprehensive production readiness or absence of semantic regressions outside the validator's scope.
